items.title: US rejects Iran's claim that warship sunk by torpedo was unarmed

featured_image.name: US submarine sinks Iranian warship off Sri Lanka killing at ...

items.description:
A U.S. Navy submarine torpedoed and sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean on March 4, killing at least 84 sailors in what marked the first American submarine attack on an enemy warship since World War II. Five days later, Washington and Tehran are locked in a dispute over whether the vessel was armed when it was struck, as the incident widens the U.S.-Israel-Iran conflict far beyond the Middle East.

The U.S. Indo-Pacific Command on Sunday rejected Iran's claim that the Dena was unarmed, calling the assertion "false" in a statement posted on X. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh had told reporters in New Delhi that the warship was "ceremonial" and "unarmed," saying it had been attending India's Milan 2026 naval exercise by invitation. An Indian Navy official, speaking anonymously, said the vessel was not "entirely unarmed".[1][2][3]

items.title: Kuwait's emir condemns Iran's 'brutal attack' in first address since strikes began

featured_image.name: Iran continues to strike Gulf infrastructure, hitting Kuwait ...

items.description:
Kuwait held military funerals on Monday for two interior ministry border security officers killed during ongoing Iranian strikes, as the country's leader broke his silence to condemn Tehran's assault on the Gulf state now entering its second week.

Lieutenant Colonel Abdullah Emad Al-Sharrah and Major Fahad Abdulaziz Al-Mejmed, both from the General Administration of Land Border Security, were buried at Sulaibikhat Cemetery in a ceremony led by First Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef Al-Sabah. The Interior Ministry said the two men were "martyred at dawn" on Sunday but did not provide further details on the circumstances of their deaths.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran rebuffs France's plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Iran Threatens 'Severe' Response to US Sanctions Against Larijani

items.description: Iran's top security official dismissed France's plans to organize a naval mission to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, warning that no security arrangement can succeed while the war ignited by the United States and Israel continues to rage across the Middle East.

items.title: CENTCOM denies Patriot misfire, blames Iranian drone for Bahrain civilian injuries

featured_image.name: State Dept. clears $2.5 billion sale of Patriot missile ...

items.description: Competing narratives emerged on Monday over what caused damage to a residential neighborhood in Manama, Bahrain, with the United States and Iran offering sharply different accounts of an incident that injured dozens of civilians amid the ongoing military conflict in the region.

items.title: IAEA chief says Iran's enriched uranium likely survived strikes at Isfahan

featured_image.name: Meet IAEA chief Rafael Grossi: The man central to the Iran ...

items.description:
Nearly half of Iran's uranium enriched to 60% purity — just short of weapons-grade — appears to have survived months of military strikes, stored deep inside a tunnel complex at Isfahan that withstood the initial US-Israeli bombing campaign last June, the head of the United Nations nuclear watchdog said Monday.

Rafael Grossi, director general of the International Atomic Energy Agency, told reporters in Paris that his agency believes "slightly more than 200 kg, possibly a bit more" of 60% enriched uranium was at Isfahan at the time of the last IAEA inspection before the June 2025 strikes. That material, he said, is probably still there.[1]

"The prevailing assumption is that the material remains there. We have not observed — and not just us, but generally all observers utilizing satellite imagery and other methods to monitor the facility — any signs of movement that would suggest the material has been transferred," Grossi said, according to Reuters.[1]

items.title: IRGC vows only one-ton warheads, wider strikes as Iran-Israel war continues

featured_image.name: Iran's IRGC: Only one-ton warhead missiles from now

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared on Monday that it will exclusively launch missiles carrying warheads weighing over one ton, a move that threatens to intensify an already devastating conflict with the United States and Israel now entering its tenth day.

Brig. Gen. Majid Mousavi, commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, said the force and frequency of Iranian missile launches would increase and attacks would broaden in scope. "From now on, no missiles will be launched with warheads lighter than 1 ton," Mousavi said, according to remarks carried by Iran's state-run Islamic Republic News Agency. The announcement came hours after Mojtaba Khamenei was named Iran's new supreme leader following the killing of his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in US-Israeli strikes.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Historic oil disruption from Iran war fuels global renewable energy push

featured_image.name: Iran vows to burn ships in Strait of Hormuz, spike oil ...

items.description:
The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, now in its tenth day, has produced the largest oil supply disruption in history and is fueling a renewed global push toward renewable energy as governments and investors reckon with the vulnerability of fossil fuel dependence.

Since coordinated strikes on Iran began on February 28, crude oil prices have surged past $100 per barrel, with roughly 20 percent of global oil and natural gas supply suspended as Tehran's retaliatory attacks have effectively shut down the Strait of Hormuz. The blockade has forced Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Iraq, and Kuwait to halt shipments of approximately 140 million barrels of oil, while Qatar declared force majeure on its liquefied natural gas exports — which account for 20 percent of the global LNG supply — after Iranian drone strikes damaged facilities.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Nvidia readies open-source AI agent platform ahead of GTC

featured_image.name: Nvidia Is Planning to Launch an Open-Source AI Agent ...

items.description:
Nvidia is preparing to launch an open source platform for AI agents, according to a report by WIRED journalists Zoë Schiffer and Lauren Goode, as the chipmaker looks to capitalize on surging enterprise interest in autonomous AI tools.[1][2]

The platform, referred to internally as NemoClaw, is being pitched to major enterprise software companies and would allow businesses to deploy AI agents that perform tasks on behalf of their employees. Notably, access to the platform would not be limited to companies running Nvidia's own chips.[3][4][5]

items.title: NASA to share Artemis II flight readiness review ahead of April launch

featured_image.name: NASA Artemis II Mission: First Crewed Moon Flyby in Over 50 Years Set for  March

items.description: NASA is ramping up public engagement for its Artemis II mission, releasing a new real-time tracking platform and scheduling a news conference this week to update the public on progress toward sending four astronauts around the Moon for the first time in more than half a century.

items.title: Putin pitches Iran peace plan to Trump, backs new supreme leader

featured_image.name: US envoys headed to Moscow to discuss Ukraine peace plan with Putin

items.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone with U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday and presented proposals for a swift end to the war in Iran, while separately pledging "unwavering support" to the country's newly appointed Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

The hourlong call, initiated by Trump, covered the Iran conflict, Ukraine, Venezuela, and global oil markets, according to Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov, who described the conversation as "businesslike, frank, and constructive".[1][2]

items.title: Around 40 killed in US-Israeli strikes on Tehran residential area, Iran says

featured_image.name: Iran says 1,255 people killed in US-Israeli attacks, mostly civilians

items.description: US and Israeli forces bombed residential blocks near Resalat Square in Tehran late Monday, killing around 40 people, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency as reported by Anadolu Agency. The strikes hit several high-rise buildings in the Iranian capital, with the death toll expected to rise as search and rescue operations continue.[1][2]

items.title: Nearly 700,000 displaced in Lebanon as Israel-Hezbollah war enters second week

featured_image.name: Israeli attacks, threats fuel mass displacement crisis in southern Lebanon

items.description: Nearly 700,000 people, including around 200,000 children, have been forced from their homes across Lebanon as the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah enters its second week, the United Nations Children's Fund said on Monday. The displacement adds to tens of thousands already uprooted from previous escalations, UNICEF said, as Israeli airstrikes expanded across southern Lebanon, the Bekaa Valley, and Beirut's southern suburbs.[1][2]

items.title: Explosion damages historic synagogue in Belgian city of Liège

featured_image.name: European countries on alert after blasts near a Belgian synagogue and outside US Embassy in Oslo

items.description:
An explosion struck a synagogue in the Belgian city of Liège early Monday morning, shattering windows and damaging the building's entrance in what officials swiftly condemned as an antisemitic attack. No injuries were reported, but the blast, which occurred around 4 a.m. local time, also blew out windows in a building across the street, according to Reuters.[1]

Belgium's federal prosecutor's office has taken charge of the investigation, telling The Jerusalem Post that there were indications the explosion was a terrorist offense. A specialized counterterrorism team and the Belgian Explosive Ordnance Disposal service were deployed to the scene, while police cordoned off the predominantly residential street along the Meuse River.[2][1]

items.title: Israel vows to target Iran's new supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei

featured_image.name: Iran names Mojtaba Khamenei as its new supreme leader

items.description: Israel has escalated its rhetoric against Iran's newly appointed supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, with senior officials and the military declaring him a target for elimination just hours after his selection was announced on March 8 by Iranian state television. The warnings mark a sharp intensification of the conflict now entering its second week, as Israeli forces continue striking targets across Iran and Lebanon.[1][2]

items.title: IRGC offers Hormuz passage to nations that expel US, Israeli envoys

featured_image.name: Navy 'tracks' Iranian ships with unmanned systems in Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Monday offered passage through the Strait of Hormuz, starting Tuesday, to any Arab or European country that expels Israeli and U.S. ambassadors from its territory, according to Shafaq News. The proposal marks a new front in Tehran's diplomatic pressure campaign as its war with the United States and Israel enters a second week.[1]

items.title: UC San Diego study finds most pandemics show no lab origins

featured_image.name: Scientists discover key clue in pandemic viruses that reveal if they were made in a lab... including Covid and 'Russian flu'

items.description: Two studies published in the past week offer fresh perspectives on viral threats — one revealing how coronaviruses rewire human cells to speed their own replication, and another providing a genomic tool to distinguish natural outbreaks from lab-linked ones, with new molecular evidence that the 1977 "Russian flu" pandemic likely originated from a failed vaccine trial.

items.title: RAF Typhoons down two drones over Jordan and Bahrain

featured_image.name: RAF Typhoon shoots down Iranian drone heading towards Qatari ...

items.description: British RAF Typhoon fighter jets shot down two drones overnight, one over Jordan and another heading toward Bahrain, as the United Kingdom expanded its defensive military operations across the Gulf on the tenth day of the war between Iran and a US-Israeli coalition.

items.title: Trump calls Iran's choice of Mojtaba Khamenei 'a big mistake'

featured_image.name: Worst-case scenario': Trump weighs replacing Khamenei as ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Monday sharply condemned Iran's selection of Mojtaba Khamenei as its new supreme leader, telling NBC News that the country "made a big mistake" and casting doubt on whether the appointment would endure. "I don't know if it's going to last ... I think they made a mistake," Trump said in a phone interview.[1][2]

In a separate interview with the New York Post, Trump said he was "not happy" with the 56-year-old cleric replacing his father. "Not going to tell you. I'm not happy with him," Trump said from his Doral golf club near Miami when asked about his plans regarding the younger Khamenei.[3][4]

items.title: Iran says it does not want to harm 'ordinary Americans'

featured_image.name: An interview with Iran's foreign minister

items.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared on Monday that Tehran does not wish to harm ordinary American citizens, framing the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict as a war driven by Israel and its allies in Washington rather than a quarrel with the American public.

"Iran does not want to harm ordinary Americans who overwhelmingly voted to end involvement in costly foreign wars," Araghchi wrote in a post on X. "Blame for surging gas prices, costlier mortgages, and pummeled 401(k)'s lies squarely with Israel and its dupes in Washington."[1]

items.title: Trump doesn't rule out seizing Iranian oil as prices spike

featured_image.name: Trump says buying Iranian oil must stop, threatens secondary ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Monday declined to rule out the possibility that the United States could seize Iranian oil as the war against Tehran enters its second week, telling NBC News that "certainly, people have talked about it" while stopping short of endorsing such a move.[1][2]

"People have thought about it, but it's too soon to talk about that," Trump said, pointing to Venezuela as a precedent where the U.S. moved to secure oil access after American forces captured President Nicolás Maduro in January. Trump touted the Venezuela operation during last month's State of the Union address, saying the U.S. had already obtained more than 80 million barrels of Venezuelan oil.[2]
